start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:turn-what-you-said-into-content on this: <paste a message, voice note transcript or talk you gave>." It decides whether the words are worth sharing, pulls out the principles in them, writes each as a story and every format that fits, keeps the drafts as rows of your content list, and feeds each principle back into your workflows.

lists.label: Principles
lists.holds: One principle per row, with every name and number taken out, the person's own words that carry it and a different field where it still holds.

values.principle: People start when they are handed something already filled in, not when they are told how to fill it in.
values.their_words: give them the rows, don't tell them instructions
values.holds_in: Teaching cooking: hand over a prepped mise en place, not a recipe card.

values.principle: A missing step said out loud is worth more than a finished-looking result that hides it.
values.their_words: say what's missing, don't pretend it's done
values.holds_in: Home inspections: the report lists what could not be reached.

alike: a notes app folder of ideas

lists.label: Content drafts
lists.holds: One drafted piece per row: its format, the goal it serves, its source, its status and the file that holds the draft.

values.piece: Stop writing instructions. Hand people the rows.

alike: a Trello board of post ideas

instructions: 1. Pour the example rows into the content calendar you already keep (see pour), or make list:content-drafts and list:principles from them.
2. Paste what you said, word for word, and say where it came from: "Run workflow:turn-what-you-said-into-content on this, from my voice note of today: ...".
3. Answer may_post only if these may be posted; otherwise every piece stays a Draft.
4. Read the principles it found (list:principles) and the drafts it kept (list:content-drafts, files under /Content/); set each draft you like to Approved.
5. Read its loop step: each principle names the workflow or check it was added to and the real work it was tried on.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and one kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
